ingredients.item: spinach, mature bunched , roots trimmed, washed twice

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Pot of unsalted water at a rolling boil, spinach in by the handful, stems first (hold the bunch tops-down, stems in the water twenty seconds, then plunge the leaves). Sixty to ninety seconds total — no more, the leaves cook in the time it takes to stir them under.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the leaves go vivid and just-wilted, stems bright and beginning to bend. Pull at vivid — the color at the pot is the color at the table, minus what overcooking steals.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Straight into cold water to shock, then — the technique — squeeze by the fistful, hard. The spinach must leave the colander as compressed, nearly dry bundles; a wet spinach bowl is a diluted one. Roughly chop the squeezed bundles once or twice.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a squeezed bundle holds its shape in the hand and drips not at all. This squeezing is the entire difference between restaurant namul and the sad watery version.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Season while the spinach is still faintly warm: sesame oil, salt, garlic, soy, sesame — tossed by hand, loosened to a bowl.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the taste: sesame-nut first, the green's mineral sweetness, garlic's hum, salt just behind. It should taste seasoned-through, not dressed-on-top — if the first bite is plain spinach and the second is garlic, the toss was short.

storageNotes: Keeps 2 days refrigerated (the color holds because it was shocked); refresh at serving with a drop of sesame oil and a re-toss.
Variations: a pinch of gochugaru for color; blanched bean sprouts folded through (#B05's lane) for the two-green bowl; the same law on blanched chives, the pattern (#B16, #B17) continues.
